lessons.title: What are you wearing today?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone. My name is Jill and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, what are you wearing today?

I'm actually really excited to answer this question because I am wearing my new favorite T-shirt, and it is from my most recent holiday. It is the shade of green that I love the most because it reminds me of the forest, and it says on here, you can either fight it or ride it, and it has a picture of a girl who is riding a wave, which is perfect because on this holiday I went on a surfing camp. I'm also wearing today a necklace that I always wear with me. And this necklace is really special because one thing about me is that I love to travel, and on this necklace are little trinkets, which I have collected from all of my travels. For example, the shell is from Spain. This little glass pendant is from Italy, and this silver key is from India. And I am wearing this today, and I wear this every day because it reminds me of happy memories that I had from when I was traveling.

What about you? What are you wearing today?

And do they hold any special meaning to you?
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
trinkets

Meaning: Small decorative objects that are not very expensive.

Examples:

  1. She wears trinkets she bought while traveling.
  2. The market was full of colorful trinkets.

necklace

Meaning: A piece of jewelry worn around the neck.

Examples:

  1. She wears a necklace every day.
  2. His gift to her was a gold necklace.

shade

Meaning: A particular type or degree of a color.

Examples:

  1. Her shirt is a shade of green she loves the most.
  2. That shade of blue looks great on you.

riding a wave

Meaning: Standing or lying on a surfboard and moving on top of a wave.

Examples:

  1. The picture shows a girl riding a wave.
  2. He learned how to ride a wave at surfing camp.

pendant

Meaning: A small decorative object hanging from a necklace.

Examples:

  1. The pendant on her necklace is made of glass.
  2. He gave her a silver pendant from Italy.

hold special meaning

Meaning: To be personally important or emotionally valuable.

Examples:

  1. These trinkets hold special meaning from my travels.
  2. The ring holds special meaning because it was a gift.

lessons.title: Is trash recycled in your country?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hi, my name is Sarah. I come from England, and my question is, is trash recycled in your country?

So the answer to that is yes. We definitely do recycle in England. It is starting to thankfully get a lot more serious and, you know, people are really starting to recycle more, especially since now, I think that you can be fined quite a lot of money if you don't recycle properly in the U.K. As of now, I think we have three different types of trash that mainly get recycled: plastic, glass, and cardboard, I believe are the three different things that we recycle right now.

We also have, like, three different trash cans, which are different colors to help you remember which type of trash goes into which type of trash can. And yeah, then the garbage guy will come and collect it, take it away, and they are separated, which makes it easier to recycle and to better help the environment.

So yeah, we definitely do recycle in England.

since

Meaning: From a time in the past until now; because.

Examples:

  1. People recycle more since new rules started.
  2. I’ve lived here since 2010.

thankfully

Meaning: Happily or luckily; used when something good has happened.

Examples:

  1. Thankfully, people are recycling more now.
  2. Thankfully, it didn’t rain during the cleanup.

definitely

Meaning: Certainly; without any doubt.

Examples:

  1. We definitely recycle in England.
  2. I definitely agree with you.

cardboard

Meaning: Thick, stiff paper used to make boxes.

Examples:

  1. We recycle cardboard with paper and boxes.
  2. The package was made of cardboard.

fined

Meaning: Made to pay money as a punishment.

Examples:

  1. You can be fined if you don’t recycle properly.
  2. He was fined for parking in the wrong place.

properly

Meaning: In the right or correct way.

Examples:

  1. Please recycle properly by using the right bin.
  2. The machine didn’t work properly.

Love Actually is a Christmas romantic comedy film. lessons.title: What did you do last night?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi everyone. My name is Jill and I'm from Australia. And my question today is, what did you do last night?

I had a really fun night last night. I got to meet with some friends that I hadn't seen in a while, so my friend cooked dinner for us, and so we went to her place and we sat together, we ate all of the food, and we talked, we laughed and we danced a little all through the night. She made a beautiful dish with mushroom rice and chicken and potatoes, and afterwards we helped clean, so we vacuumed her living room. We cleaned the dishes, and then we decided that we wanted some dessert. And so we walked to the nearest bubble tea shop where we laughed so much that we were scared we were going to get kicked out, but we didn't. And so we sat, we laughed, we talked, and then I had to say goodnight and come home for the evening.

What about you? What did you do last night? Did you do anything fun?
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
vacuumed

Meaning: Cleaned the floor using a machine that sucks up dust and dirt.

Examples:

  1. We vacuumed the living room after dinner.
  2. She vacuumed her house before the guests arrived.

all through the night

Meaning: For the entire night; from evening until morning.

Examples:

  1. We talked and danced all through the night.
  2. It rained all through the night.

afterwards

Meaning: After something has happened; later.

Examples:

  1. We cleaned the kitchen afterwards.
  2. Afterwards, we went out for dessert.

get kicked out

Meaning: To be forced to leave a place because of bad behavior or breaking rules.

Examples:

  1. They laughed so much they almost got kicked out of the café.
  2. He got kicked out of class for being noisy.

bubble tea

Meaning: A sweet drink with milk or fruit flavor and small chewy balls called tapioca pearls.

Examples:

  1. We went to a bubble tea shop after dinner.
  2. She ordered a large bubble tea with brown sugar pearls.

in a while

Meaning: For a long time; recently not.

Examples:

  1. I hadn’t seen my friends in a while.
  2. We haven’t eaten out in a while.

Well, when I was younger, I really loved a sport called kicking ball. It's like baseball, but instead of hitting, it's kicking with foot, it's really fun. I played that sport for years. Right now, I don't play those sports, but I go to the gym every single day, you know, lifting weights. I do CrossFit. I do functional training. lessons.title: Do you belong to a group or community?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hi. My name is Nev, and I'm from Canada. My question for today is do you belong to a group or community?

And unfortunately I don't, not because I have anything about being a part of a group or community. It's only because I've been traveling a lot over the past six years now. So I haven't really had the chance to be somewhere long enough to become a member of a group or part of a community.

If I were to become one, and hopefully I will in the future, I would like to join communities that help people around us, communities that offer services for let's say homeless people or people who are struggling when it comes to their mental health or things like that. So I think it would be great to give something back to the community and to be a part of something useful.

What do you think? Would you consider being a part of a community? Unless you already are.

let’s say

Meaning: Used to give an example or imagine a situation.

  1. Let’s say you move to a new city. How would you make friends?
  2. Let’s say it rains tomorrow — we’ll stay inside.

when it comes to

Meaning: Used to talk about a specific topic or situation.

Examples:

  1. When it comes to cooking, she’s the best in the family.
  2. He’s very careful when it comes to money.

things like that

Meaning: Used to talk about similar examples without listing all of them.

Examples:

  1. I enjoy hiking, camping, and things like that.
  2. They talked about school, work, and things like that.

give something back

Meaning: To do something to help or thank a person or community.

Examples:

  1. He volunteers to give something back to the community.
  2. She wants to give something back after getting so much support.

had the chance

Meaning: Had the opportunity or time to do something.

Examples:

  1. I haven’t had the chance to visit my friends lately.
  2. She finally had the chance to see the concert.

lessons.title: What do you usually eat for dinner?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Lilith and I'm from Armenia. Today, my question is, what do you usually eat for dinner?

Here in Armenia, we have lots of traditional dishes which are made with meat and are really delicious, but somehow I happen not to like them. It's probably because all my childhood I've eaten Armenian traditional food, and I have grown to dislike this kind of food.

So now that I'm lucky to be living alone, I can cook whatever I like. I'm really fond of Italian food. So for dinner, I usually have either a pasta with some different types of sauce, or some soup, sometimes mashed potatoes with steak, and occasionally pizza. I really like seafood and fish. So from time to time, I make some new dishes which include seafood, or fried fish, or fish and chips, and things like that.

lessons.title: How often do you use public tranportation?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

How often do I use public transport?

Pretty much never these days. I recently moved to New Orleans, as we pronounce it here, New Orleans. New Orleans, Louisiana: NOLA.

There's very limited public transport in New Orleans. There's a great street car, a tram, as I would call it. But I'm more of a walker. I love walking. If something's close enough, I'll walk there. And having recently had a baby and things being quite far away in New Orleans, we had to buy a car. I haven't driven a car since I was in Japan about 10 years ago. But a car is kind of essential here.

When I'm in other cities, I do like to walk, or get public transportation. I love trains and long distance buses, but unfortunately reality nowadays means that in a big city like New Orleans, I need to drive a car. So I do.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
public transport / public transportation

Meaning: Buses, trains, subways, trams, and other transport available to everyone.

Examples:

  1. I rarely use public transport in New Orleans.
  2. Public transportation is very convenient in big cities.

pronounce

Meaning: To say a word in a particular way.

Examples:

  1. We pronounce it “New Or-lins” here.
  2. She can’t pronounce his name correctly.

street car / tram

Meaning: A small train that runs on tracks in city streets.

Examples:

  1. New Orleans has a famous street car.
  2. I took a tram to the city center.

quite

Meaning: Very; to a large degree.

Examples:

  1. Things are quite far apart in New Orleans.
  2. It’s quite difficult to find a bus here.

essential

Meaning: Very important or necessary.

Examples:

  1. Having a car is essential in New Orleans.
  2. Water is essential for good health.

unfortunately

Meaning: Sadly; used when something is disappointing.

Examples:

  1. Unfortunately, public transport isn’t great here.
  2. Unfortunately, I missed the last bus.

reality means that

Meaning: In real life, the situation forces something to happen.

Examples:

  1. Unfortunately, reality means that I need a car now.
  2. Reality means that not everyone can walk to work.

nowadays

Meaning: At the present time; in modern times.

Examples:

  1. Nowadays, many cities require people to drive.
  2. Public transport is more popular nowadays.

lessons.title: What are the best and worst parts of your job?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

The question that I'm answering is, is what are the best and worst parts of your job?

Currently, the main job that I do is provide voiceovers, and whether that be for YouTube videos or commercials, I provide the voice behind it.

So, one of the best parts of this job is that having so many scripts to narrate for different channels, I get to learn a lot. I've learnt about the facts about space. I've learnt financial hints and tips. I've learnt about travel destinations. I've learnt about sports. Basically, anything that I get to read, I get to learn.

The worst part about this is sometimes not being able to pronounce names and places properly. Because my main language is English, if I get a place or a name that's German or Russian or from Cambodia, I find it very difficult to pronounce, and I often have to go onto YouTube or go onto the internet to find out how to pronounce it correctly.

Meaning: Places that people go to for vacations or trips.

Examples:

  2. We talked about our favorite travel destinations.

go onto

Meaning: To visit or move to another website or platform online.

Examples:

  1. I often go onto YouTube to watch videos.
  2. He went onto the website to find the answer.

not being able to

Meaning: When something is too hard or impossible for someone to do.

Examples:

  1. Not being able to pronounce words is frustrating.
  2. She hates not being able to help her friends.

whether that be

Meaning: Used to give examples of different possibilities.

Examples:

  1. I record many things, whether that be ads or videos.
  2. She enjoys reading, whether that be novels or magazines.

get to

Meaning: To have the chance or opportunity to do something.

Examples:

  1. I get to learn something new every day.
  2. We get to meet people from many countries.

lessons.title: Would you like to have a dangerous job?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hi. My name is Nev and I come from Canada. For today my question is would you like to have a dangerous job?

To be honest, this is an easy question, and my answer is no. I wouldn't like to have a dangerous job. I work as a kindergarten teacher, and to be honest, I love my job. So, if I were to change it, I still wouldn't consider doing anything that's dangerous to me or people around me.

Why?

That would be an interesting thing to explain. Maybe because I think I wouldn't be able to do such a job because I'm very sensitive, and if I see someone in pain or in any kind of trouble that could potentially seriously hurt or damage him, I don't think I would be able to deal with all that on a daily basis. And job is something that you do every day so we might as well like it. That's why I'm keeping mine.

What about you? Would you consider changing your job and having a dangerous one?
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
to be honest

Meaning: Used to show that you are giving your real opinion or telling the truth.

Examples:

  1. To be honest, I don’t like dangerous jobs.
  2. To be honest, I was very nervous before the interview.

on a daily basis

Meaning: Every day; regularly each day.

Examples:

  1. Teachers deal with students on a daily basis.
  2. I exercise on a daily basis to stay healthy.

like to have

Meaning: To want or enjoy having something.

Examples:

  1. I wouldn’t like to have a dangerous job.
  2. She would like to have more free time.

might as well

Meaning: Used to suggest doing something because there is no good reason not to.

Examples:

  1. We might as well like our job if we do it every day.
  2. It’s raining, so we might as well stay inside.

deal with all

Meaning: To handle or manage everything that happens in a situation.

Examples:

  1. I couldn’t deal with all the stress of a dangerous job.
  2. Parents have to deal with all kinds of problems.

Vocabulary Quiz

lessons.title: What colors do you like and dislike to wear?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Veronica, and I'm from the United States. My question today is what colors do you like and dislike to wear?

Obviously, one of the colors that I like to wear is blue. I think it's my favorite color to wear because I feel like it suits my skin tone very well. Since I have a lighter skin tone and darker hair, I feel like blue looks very good on me. Sometimes I wear a muted blue like I am today. Sometimes I wear a very bright, like a royal blue. Either one of those I think really looks nice on me, and so it is actually my favorite color to wear.

My least favorite color to wear is yellow. You won't find a lot of yellow in my wardrobe. And the only reason is I think yellow is a beautiful color. It is bright. It is captivating and it looks so good on so many people. I just don't feel like yellow looks good on me. So it is very rare that you will ever see me wearing the color yellow.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
muted

Meaning: Soft or not bright in color; gentle in tone.

Examples:

  1. She wore a muted blue shirt today.
  2. The walls were painted in muted colors.

very rare

Meaning: Not common; happening only sometimes.

Examples:

  1. It is very rare to see her wearing yellow.
  2. Snow is very rare in this area.

wardrobe

Meaning: The collection of clothes that people wear.

Examples:

  1. You won't find the color yellow in my wardrobe.
  2. She spends a lot of money on her wardrobe.

captivating

Meaning: Very interesting or beautiful in a way that holds your attention.

Examples:

  1. Yellow is a bright and captivating color.
  2. The movie was so captivating that I watched it twice.

it suits

Meaning: Looks good on someone; matches their appearance or style.

Examples:

  1. I feel like blue suits my skin tone well.
  2. That dress really suits you.

I feel like

Meaning: I think or believe; used to express a personal opinion or feeling.

Examples:

  1. I feel like blue looks very good on me.
  2. I feel like today is going to be a great day.

Hello, my name is Lilit. I'm from Armenia. Today my question is, do you have piercings?

I absolutely love piercings. Although I have piercings only on my ears, but I have this little tradition of getting a piercing every time I accomplish something my life. So most of my piercings I got during my student years, when I graduated college, then I graduated university, when I got my first job, which was a big accomplishment for me at that time. So I think it's a really fun way for me to commemorate all these achievements that I have in my life.

And I'm thinking I will continue doing this in the future as well and maybe one day I'll have my ears fully pierced. So I think that if anyone is thinking of getting a piercing, they should absolutely do it because it's just as fun as getting a tattoo or something similar.

lessons.title: What do you usually eat for lunch?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hide / Show Transcript

Hello. My name is Veronica, and I'm from the United States. And my question today is, what do you usually eat for lunch?

Well, get ready because my answer might be a little bit boring for you. I usually eat the same thing for lunch every day, and it's normally a salad. And the reason why I eat the same thing for lunch every day is because it's a lot easier to do that, plus, I try to have a healthier lifestyle.

So for me, if I'm eating a salad at lunch every day, I know that I'm getting the amount of vegetables and fruits that I need throughout my day, plus I don't have a lot of time to sit down and actually eat a big meal, so for me if I'm able to stop and have something healthy and refreshing, it's not going to slow me down. I know that there are a lot of cultures that believe in eating a big meal at lunch. But if I were to eat, say for example, a big steak and a potato, I would need a nap right afterwards, so normally I just have a salad for lunch every day so that I can stay healthy and keep going.

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hello, my name is Preah, and I am from Belize. My question is, what was your most embarrassing moment?

So when I was 18 years old, I decided that I wanted to move to Mexico. I was an adult, and I felt like I could do anything I wanted. I also thought that I knew Spanish, but I quickly learned that I didn't know as much as I thought. So I was at this mall and there was this man. He was doing a play, and he wanted to invite me on stage as a part of his play.

And I kept telling him in Spanish, "Soy embarazado. Soy embarazado."

And I thought that I was saying, "I'm embarrassed" because "embarazado - embarrassed" I thought they meant the same thing.

And he kept telling me, "congratulations, congratulations."

And I was like, "no, soy embarazado."

And he kept saying, "congratulations, boy or girl?"

And I was like, "I am a girl," I told him.

It wasn't until afterwards I realized, or I learned that "embarazado" or "embarazada" meant pregnant and embarrassed, what I actually wanted to say, meant "avergonzado," right?

So that was pretty embarrassing because everyone thought that I was pregnant, but I actually wanted to say that I was embarrassed.

lessons.title: How do you feel about having a pet?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Ozlem, and I'm from Turkey. Here is my question: How do you feel about having a pet?

Having a pet brings a circle of love into our lives. This is certain, and I remember reading an article about human and animal connection, and in that article, there were around ten health benefits, like lower depression, blood rates, more physical activity, and so on. Yes, they are definitely good for humans.

We all love him very much, and we try to spend time with him. But on the contrary, I sometimes feel guilty about him because I cannot spend so much time with him, so that makes me sad.

Yes, as a result, having a pet is definitely good for humans. But the question is, are we good for them?

lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.

The question that I'm answering is did you have a part-time job when you were younger?

The answer to this is I've had a few part-time jobs, but I'll talk about my first part-time job, which is delivering the newspaper. lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi. I'm Ozlem and I'm from Turkey. Here is my question: Who do you speak English with?

I work as an ESL teacher in a private school here in Turkey. At school, as a general rule, we do not speak our native language because we believe our students should be surrounded by the second language they learn, which is English in our case. So, we try to speak English everywhere anytime we are with them. In the process of language learning, there are four skills students should acquire: Reading, writing, listening, and speaking, and speaking is the productive skill. This means if students, if they need to improve this skill, they need to produce.

Anyway, apart from that, I have many other colleagues and native friends, so we always speak English together. But if you do not have people around you speaking English, you can also find friends online or you can have an English tutor to practice online. That's it. Thank you and see you. Bye.

Have you ever had a beloved pet?

I've actually always been a dog person and I've always wanted a dog, but I never really got one up until now. So now I have, I would like to say small puppy, but he is not that small. He's Belgian Shepherd, a Malinois, and he's becoming very big, which is an increasing problem in our household.

What is my dream job?

Okay, so my dream job is to become a successful business woman. I don't call it a dream job, I just call it a goal. This is my goal to become successful business woman. But apart from this, I love trading a lot. I would die to become pro at scalping trading. This is what I'm actually willing to be doing in the next few months, learning more about trading and scalping, and this is what I'm willing to be successful at one day, you know. So, I always imagine myself, I don't mind if I see it the whole day in front of my screen doing scalping, learning new things, learning more about it.

So yeah, this is actually what I'm willing to be doing in the next few months and few years. So, yeah, that's it.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

the whole day

Meaning: All day long; from morning to night.

Examples:

  1. I spent the whole day studying for my exam.
  2. He was so tired because he worked the whole day without a break.

I’ll call it

Meaning: A way to introduce how you describe or name something.

Examples:

  1. It’s not really a job, but I’ll call it a side hustle.
  2. I don’t know if it's a skill, but I’ll call it a talent.

But apart from

Meaning: Besides; in addition to something.

Examples:

  1. But apart from English, I also want to learn Spanish.
  2. He works as a teacher, but apart from that, he also writes books.

would die to

Meaning: A strong way to say you really want something.

Examples:

  1. I would die to travel the world and see new places.
  2. She would die to meet her favorite actor in person.

pro at

Meaning: Very skilled at something; professional level.

Examples:

  1. He is pro at playing video games and wins every match.
  2. She wants to be pro at public speaking to give better presentations.

willing to

Meaning: Ready or happy to do something.

Examples:

  1. I am willing to work extra hours to finish this project.
  2. She is willing to help anyone who asks.

lessons.title: What are some tips in language learning?
lessons.description: One Minute English video lesson for Intermediate learners.
lessons.transcriptHtml:
Hi, I'm Ozlem. I'm from Turkey. And here is my question: what are some tips in language learning?

I have been an ESL teacher for over 20 years, and I would like to say a few things about language learning. I always see people trying to find a shortcut in language learning. Yes, you can have a shortcut in the sense of time, but I don't believe you can have a shortcut in the sense of effort. So, number one, you should find the reason: why do you want to learn this language? For example, if you want to speak fluently, you should focus on speaking and listening activities. I generally see people complaining about the amount of time they have spent and have no result at the end. But when we look closer at their studies, we see that they have not spent enough time in that specific skill they want. And secondly, you should follow a system. If you follow a system, if you have a system, and thirdly, if you have fun, this is very important, you will definitely learn the language. So have a system and have fun. Love what you are doing. Thank you. See you later. Bye.
lessons.vocabularyHtml:
How to Practice Vocabulary

  • Review the vocabulary.
  • Complete the blanks below with correct words.
  • Check your answers. Correct any wrong answers!

focus on

Meaning: To give attention to something.

Examples:

  1. You should focus on improving your speaking skills.
  2. Instead of multitasking, focus on one thing at a time.

generally

Meaning: Usually; most of the time.

Examples:

  1. I generally wake up early, but sometimes I sleep in on weekends.
  2. People generally learn a new language faster if they practice daily.

say a few things

Meaning: To briefly talk about something.

Examples:

  1. Before we begin, I want to say a few things about today's lesson.
  2. She stood up to say a few things about her experience.

follow a system

Meaning: To use a planned method or structure to do something.

Examples:

  1. If you follow a system, learning a language becomes easier.
  2. Successful businesses follow a system to stay organized.

in the sense of

Meaning: When explaining something in a specific way or meaning.

Examples:

  1. He is rich in the sense of having many friends, not money.
  2. The book is difficult in the sense of using advanced vocabulary.

shortcut

Meaning: A faster or easier way to do something.

Examples:

  1. There is no shortcut to learning a language; you need to practice.
  2. He took a shortcut through the park to save time.

at the end

Meaning: When something is finished or completed.

Examples:

  1. At the end of the movie, the main character finds true love.
  2. They worked hard, and at the end, they won the competition.
